Welcome, Coaches. We are pleased to introduce Fernando Sagal to the Grand Slam Coaches Conference. Fernando has more than 40 years of coaching experience, focusing much of this time in the tennis development realm and known globally for his philosophical concepts around coach development and increasing participation to create a continuous, educational and developmental pathway for coaches, players, parents, managers and tennis organisations. He is the author of 11 published books on different tennis topics and has lectured on his concepts and theories at a variety of ITF World Conferences, National Tennis Congresses and in more than 45 countries. Please welcome Fernando as he talks us through transition as a methodological concept. Over to you, Fernando. Hi, everyone. It's a pleasure for me, Fernando Sagal, to be in the Australian Grand Slam Conference presenting to you about the meaning of transition as a methodological concept. One of the key aspects to understand in terms of my presentation is about the principles of my book FFS, which means analytic formative system, which means always manage the internal and external resources that are required in any situation. From my point of view, it's very important that coaches, when you are working with players, you have to be very disciplinated on how you are creating an environment of learning, on the learning process of your player.
